IBM Support for Java 6 with Business Process Manager and Business Monitor ending April 2018 - United States

FLASH (ALERT)

ABSTRACT
 Support for Java 6 on WebSphere Application Server ended on April 30th, 2018. There will not be any extended support available for Java 6. Customers using Business Process Manager or Business Monitor versions prior to 8.5.6 will need to upgrade if you wish to continue running a supported Java level. 

CONTENT
For more details on supported Java levels, see BPM and Business Monitor supported Java versions [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21639640]. 

For more info on the withdrawal of Java 6 support for WAS, see the "WebSphere Application Server V8.5 Java™ support" section on the WAS software withdrawal page [https://www-01.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/3/897/ENUS916-143/index.html&request_locale=en].

If you continue to use a supported BPM or Monitor level with Java 6 past this time frame, you will still be able to get support for BPM or Monitor issues. Although you will not be able to get fixes for any Java problems or security flaws that are found in Java.

*  With this interim fix the synchronization between different
   threads will be fixed so that access to the exection context by
   multiple threads is possible.
   
   FIX AVAILABILITY:
   iFix for 7.5.1.1 is available on Fix Central, search for APAR
   JR47535 at http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/ [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/]
   Fix is also targetted for inclusion in next fixpack for BPM
   V7.5.1, BPM 8.0.1, BPM 8.5.0
   
   When obtaining any of the above fixes, be sure to download the
   accompanying readme, for itself, and any prerequisite fixes, and
   review them thorougly.
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

COMMENTS

     initOldWebWFM(ServiceRunnerManager.java:101)
   at com.ibm.bpm.rest.impl.service.ServiceRunnerManager.
     getInstance(ServiceRunnerManager.java:66)
   at com.ibm.bpm.rest.impl.service.ServiceResource.
     getServiceActions(ServiceResource.java:105)

*  This fix addresses two issues:
   - Creating a federation domain on a cluster scope is not
   working. The federation domain is always created on cell scope
   instead.
   - The admin command addBPMSystem fails with the following
   exception when there are two clusters.
   
   The appropriate check was added in the code and the federation
   domain is now created on the correct cluster level.
   
   FIX AVAILABILITY:
   
   iFix on top of BPM 8.0.1.1 is available on Fix Central,
   search for APAR JR46962 at
   http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/ [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/]
   
   Fix is also targetted for inclusion in next fixpack for BPM
   V8.0.1.2
   Fix is also targetted for inclusion in next fixpack for BPM
   V8.5.0.1
   
   When obtaining any of the above fixes, be sure to download the
   accompanying readme, for itself and any prerequisite fixes, and

   minCmdProxyBase.java

*  Problem Conclusion:
   
   The database interaction used is not supported by Oracle.
   
   The fix addresses both problems as follows:
   
   The fix changes database interaction such that Oracle supports
   it.
   
   FIX AVAILABILITY:
   
   iFix for 8.0.1.1 is available on Fix Central, search for APAR
   JR46348 at http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/ [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/]
   Fix is also targetted for inclusion in next fixpack for BPM
   8.0.1
   Fix is also included in BPM 8.5.0
   
   When obtaining any of the above fixes, be sure to download the
   accompanying readme, for itself and any prerequisite fixes, and
   review them thorougly.

   missing databaseName resource property in the custom data
   source.
